6	# STDO Review
7	
8	In the execution path, act as Reviewer for one exact claim. The reviewed subject
9	is read-only. Record findings only through the exact artifact effects the
10	selected basis and activation grant. Do not repair, assign Product priority,
11	apply disposition, or activate the next work.
12	
13	## Start With Your Own Control Intake
14	
15	Read the exact own contract or intake named in the request before any general
16	search or project read. Bind your own permitted inputs, exclusions and return
17	route, then apply [Control Intake](../../references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#control-intake).
18	This applies to issuer, recipient and direct work. Use named control routes;
19	do not start with directory inventories, memory searches or neighbouring
20	prompts. A Worker’s access never becomes its issuer’s access. Check the actual
21	host boundary before relying on excluded information staying unavailable.
22	
23	## Choose The Entry
24	
25	If receiving a coordinated packet, apply
26	[Receive](../../references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#receive) before general
27	discovery or candidate reads, then execute the review below within its grant.
28	
29	A coordinating issuer uses [Issue](../../references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#issue)
30	with `EXECUTIVE_BASELINE` §12 step 5B and §19's Reviewer additions. Bind the
31	exact claim, candidate, evidence population, severity scale and required
32	authorship/evidence independence. Let the Reviewer derive expectations from
33	governing source before candidate exposure (`EVALUATION` §3). Label supplied
34	hypotheses or counterexamples as inputs; they neither prescribe the verdict
35	nor replace independent assessment. Do not hide relevant evidence to create
36	an appearance of independence.
37	
38	Partition only when each Reviewer has a sufficient complete slice and the
39	declared conjunction covers the required claim, including interactions.
40	Local green slices do not prove an unassessed whole path. Evaluate returned
41	results through [the shared return procedure](../../references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#evaluate-the-return);
42	retain Reviewer severity and assign priority/disposition only under the
43	issuer's separate grant. The issuer does not perform a second review merely
44	by issuing this one. Apply [the selected review flow](../../references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#review-flow-from-the-selected-basis)
45	for coverage, proportional sizing and any recheck; do not copy the optional
46	candidate policy onto an older basis. Otherwise enter the Reviewer path below.
47	
48	## Select The Product Basis
49	
50	Read and apply
51	[`PRODUCT_BASIS.md`](../../references/PRODUCT_BASIS.md) before activating review.
52	Continue only from its exactly-one verified selection. That selection supplies
53	no artifact-write grant.
54	
55	## Activate The Review
56	
57	1. From the verified definition and installed basis, bind candidate/checkpoint,
58	   exact affected Product claims, authority, scope,
59	   exclusions, evidence population, required independence, Reviewer capability
60	   envelope, Executive baseline profile technical-triage fields where adopted, the
61	   Product-selected severity scale, review time, and invalidation under the
62	   three invalidators of `ACTIVATION.md` section 7, a subject, capability or
63	   scale change being a named instance of a material input change or a
64	   changed basis.
65	2. Reacquire live authority, implementation, tests, fixtures, installed or
66	   runtime evidence, and material history. Do not use the Worker summary as
67	   evidence. Acquire owning sections under the selected basis's
68	   `ACTIVATION.md` section 2, Acquisition; review law is `EVALUATION.md`
69	   sections 3 and 4.
70	   Reuse exact applicable computed facts and traceable prior judgments after
71	   checking their support and invalidation. This does not replace your own
72	   assessment where the claim requires independence. Determine required
73	   evaluations from the owning applicability conditions, not only the caller's
74	   selected frame list; unknown applicability or a missing required exact
75	   result prevents a satisfied conjunction.
76	3. Return the exact invalid, out-of-frame, or indeterminate result when subject,
77	   basis, capability, independence, or evidence cannot support evaluation.
78	
79	## Evaluate
80	
81	- Search for counterexamples against the claim: authority seams, rival paths,
82	  proof masking, failure/recovery, installed behavior, and reconstruction.
83	- Inspect tests, fixtures, mutations, environment, and interpretation where
84	  they can change the proof.
85	- Bind findings and affected acceptance predicates to a violated property,
86	  supported entry/state, governing operating/threat model and credible causal
87	  path. An excluded threat gives no guard a retention claim; test presence
88	  creates no authority (FOUNDATIONS §2 What creates no authority). Internal location alone does not establish trust.
89	  Preserve supported input, mutable-state, authority and effect checks.
90	- For material computational composition or recurrence, evaluate one complete
91	  producer-to-consumer path, including established facts, invalidators, effects,
92	  retained alternatives and accumulated work. Require the claimed operational
93	  observations; local passes or semantic agreement cannot establish them.
94	  Reuse still-valid support without substituting another actor's judgment for
95	  the required independent assessment.
96	- Under an adopted Executive baseline profile, return technical severity, causal
97	  assessment and confidence where supportable, blast radius, workaround or
98	  containment, repair complexity, regression risk, and residual uncertainty.
99	- Use only the Product-bound scale. Keep adjacent observations separate.
100	- When the basis selects the review flow's 1 highest–5 lowest convention, use
101	  its qualitative consequence anchors and Product evidence criteria. For
102	  severity 3, explicitly assess dependent paths and blast radius; do not call
103	  unknown impact contained or relabel an older finding's scale. The Executive
104	  still owns priority and any repair/deferral decision.
105	- Never turn technical severity into Executive priority or promotion-boundary
106	  effect. Whether a finding blocks promotion is decided by EVALUATION §5 When
107	  a finding blocks promotion.
108	- Distinguish repair of a nonconforming candidate under unchanged law from an
109	  intentional governing change. A failure alone does not require repricing.
110	- Check satisfied closure conditions; your review event cannot establish them
111	  or create an additional closing ceremony.
112	
113	Keep the result projection total over the core values of `FOUNDATIONS.md`
114	section 4, Results:
115	
116	- `satisfied`: no finding; triage is `not_applicable`;
117	- `falsified`: findings carry complete triage or explicit field-level
118	  indeterminate values;
119	- `indeterminate` or `out_of_frame`: return the unresolved triage and basis;
120	  and
121	- `invalid_basis`: triage is `not_applicable`; return the basis re-entry.
122	
123	## Return
124	
125	Return one closed result containing exact subject and basis, claim, scope and
126	exclusions, evidence, verdict, findings and counterexamples, triage, residuals,
127	adjacent observations, uncertainty, invalidation, and owning re-entry point.
128	Bind each reusable judgment to its question, subject/basis, supporting facts,
129	actor/authority, conclusion/scope and revising observation in the existing
130	result carrier. Preserve original owner rulings separately from interpretation.
131	Name any unperformed coverage. When the selected TICKETS law provides a linked
132	bug report, record it only at the exact granted identity/path, with unchanged
133	severity and inherited visibility restrictions; otherwise return it for the
134	lawful Writer. With no findings, create no bug report. Return the report link
135	without exposing withheld evidence in the surrounding summary.
136	Return to the coordination the applicable configuration selects: the
137	Executive when the Project Reference-Frame Basis adopts that frame;
138	otherwise the Product-owned decision authority. Stop.

---

# STDO Review

In the execution path, act as Reviewer for one exact claim. The reviewed subject
is read-only. Record findings only through the exact artifact effects the
selected basis and activation grant. Do not repair, assign Product priority,
apply disposition, or activate the next work.

route, then apply [Control Intake](../../references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#control-intake).

do not start with directory inventories, memory searches or neighbouring
prompts. A Worker’s access never becomes its issuer’s access. Check the actual
host boundary before relying on excluded information staying unavailable.

A coordinating issuer uses [Issue](../../references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#issue)
with `EXECUTIVE_BASELINE` §12 step 5B and §19's Reviewer additions. Bind the
exact claim, candidate, evidence population, severity scale and required
authorship/evidence independence. Let the Reviewer derive expectations from
governing source before candidate exposure (`EVALUATION` §3). Label supplied

nor replace independent assessment. Do not hide relevant evidence to create

Partition only when each Reviewer has a sufficient complete slice and the

Local green slices do not prove an unassessed whole path. Evaluate returned
results through [the shared return procedure](../../references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#evaluate-the-return);
retain Reviewer severity and assign priority/disposition only under the
issuer's separate grant. The issuer does not perform a second review merely
by issuing this one. Apply [the selected review flow](../../references/COORDINATED_HANDOFF.md#review-flow-from-the-selected-basis)
for coverage, proportional sizing and any recheck; do not copy the optional
candidate policy onto an older basis. Otherwise enter the Reviewer path below.

## Select The Product Basis

Read and apply
[`PRODUCT_BASIS.md`](../../references/PRODUCT_BASIS.md) before activating review.
Continue only from its exactly-one verified selection. That selection supplies
no artifact-write grant.

## Activate The Review

1. From the verified definition and installed basis, bind candidate/checkpoint,
   exact affected Product claims, authority, scope,
   exclusions, evidence population, required independence, Reviewer capability
   envelope, Executive baseline profile technical-triage fields where adopted, the
   Product-selected severity scale, review time, and invalidation under the
   three invalidators of `ACTIVATION.md` section 7, a subject, capability or
   scale change being a named instance of a material input change or a
   changed basis.
2. Reacquire live authority, implementation, tests, fixtures, installed or
   runtime evidence, and material history. Do not use the Worker summary as
   evidence. Acquire owning sections under the selected basis's
   `ACTIVATION.md` section 2, Acquisition; review law is `EVALUATION.md`
   sections 3 and 4.
   Reuse exact applicable computed facts and traceable prior judgments after
   checking their support and invalidation. This does not replace your own
   assessment where the claim requires independence. Determine required
   evaluations from the owning applicability conditions, not only the caller's
   selected frame list; unknown applicability or a missing required exact
   result prevents a satisfied conjunction.
3. Return the exact invalid, out-of-frame, or indeterminate result when subject,
   basis, capability, independence, or evidence cannot support evaluation.

## Evaluate

- Search for counterexamples against the claim: authority seams, rival paths,
  proof masking, failure/recovery, installed behavior, and reconstruction.
- Inspect tests, fixtures, mutations, environment, and interpretation where
  they can change the proof.
- Bind findings and affected acceptance predicates to a violated property,
  supported entry/state, governing operating/threat model and credible causal
  path. An excluded threat gives no guard a retention claim; test presence
  creates no authority (FOUNDATIONS §2 What creates no authority). Internal location alone does not establish trust.
  Preserve supported input, mutable-state, authority and effect checks.
- For material computational composition or recurrence, evaluate one complete
  producer-to-consumer path, including established facts, invalidators, effects,
  retained alternatives and accumulated work. Require the claimed operational
  observations; local passes or semantic agreement cannot establish them.
  Reuse still-valid support without substituting another actor's judgment for
  the required independent assessment.
- Under an adopted Executive baseline profile, return technical severity, causal
  assessment and confidence where supportable, blast radius, workaround or
  containment, repair complexity, regression risk, and residual uncertainty.
- Use only the Product-bound scale. Keep adjacent observations separate.
- When the basis selects the review flow's 1 highest–5 lowest convention, use
  its qualitative consequence anchors and Product evidence criteria. For
  severity 3, explicitly assess dependent paths and blast radius; do not call
  unknown impact contained or relabel an older finding's scale. The Executive
  still owns priority and any repair/deferral decision.
- Never turn technical severity into Executive priority or promotion-boundary
  effect. Whether a finding blocks promotion is decided by EVALUATION §5 When
  a finding blocks promotion.
- Distinguish repair of a nonconforming candidate under unchanged law from an
  intentional governing change. A failure alone does not require repricing.
- Check satisfied closure conditions; your review event cannot establish them
  or create an additional closing ceremony.

Keep the result projection total over the core values of `FOUNDATIONS.md`
section 4, Results:

- `satisfied`: no finding; triage is `not_applicable`;
- `falsified`: findings carry complete triage or explicit field-level
  indeterminate values;
- `indeterminate` or `out_of_frame`: return the unresolved triage and basis;
  and
- `invalid_basis`: triage is `not_applicable`; return the basis re-entry.

## Return

Return one closed result containing exact subject and basis, claim, scope and
exclusions, evidence, verdict, findings and counterexamples, triage, residuals,
adjacent observations, uncertainty, invalidation, and owning re-entry point.
Bind each reusable judgment to its question, subject/basis, supporting facts,
actor/authority, conclusion/scope and revising observation in the existing
result carrier. Preserve original owner rulings separately from interpretation.

Return to the coordination the applicable configuration selects: the
Executive when the Project Reference-Frame Basis adopts that frame;

Jim's current instruction is: “ok approved i want you to release stdo 3.1 rc???”
Remote release inspection selects the next unoccupied ordinal, 3.1.0-rc.3,
following published RC2. This authorizes construction, commits, tags, the guarded
atomic release transaction, normal GitHub publication and public verification.
The six-Product relation in requirements/RELEASE_3_1.md continues unchanged.

Root acts as the separately declared direct Writer for this bounded release:
approved Method source plus necessary exact-cut Context, Skills, visual and
manager/package identity changes, their evidence and release navigation in this
isolated checkout. It makes no Executive-role mutation or implicit sibling
capability expansion. Source-first external Claude-family reviewers assess
frozen subjects without repair. Their original architectural contribution is
disclosed; they are independent of this Codex construction, not of that direction.

Installed STDO 3.0.4 remains the construction basis. The root and child AGENTS,
Product Definitions, frame bases, native work/review skills and RELEASE 2/3/6/7/8/9
apply. No matching final-cut index exists yet; source owners govern construction.
Context indexes are derived only after actual native cut/manifest verification.

The method is self-contained. Product defines the intended end state; Goals are
current epics. Tracking and reconciliation to the authoritative mutable workspace
remain required. A generic register is an optional example; equivalent LLM or
other mechanisms are allowed. The method does not mandate a ledger, event log,
fixed evaluator API, replay architecture, or downstream product implementation.

Original main has unrelated unpushed commits and dirty work; preserve all its

effects. Exact public acquisition and fresh isolated installation close publication.
Human exact-cut acceptance and whole-method qualification remain separate claims.

224	## 5. Graph model
225	
226	The product is expressed as a declared asset graph over the state
227	transitions relevant to the product's work (P0, P3).
228	
229	### Nodes
230	
231	Nodes name bounded states of typed domain assets in the workspace. In one software-development ODD product the nodes include
232	`intent`, `product`, `requirements`, `design`, `module_decomp`, `code`,
233	`uat_testcases`, `integration_tests`, `bootloader` and build targets. Those
234	names are illustrative and product-local; the law is that nodes name
235	bounded states (P3).
236	
237	### Vectors
238	
239	Vectors are the lawful transitions between nodes and are the admissible
240	transitions of the product. Each vector declares its required upstream
241	assets, its target asset, its governing evaluators and gates, and its
242	output contract (P4a, P6).
243	
244	### Probabilistic compute
245	
246	Probabilistic compute in this profile is bounded constructive work over
247	one declared vector or edge traversal, where the graph or runtime does not
248	fully determine the worker's internal solution path. One vector or edge
249	traversal is the bounded unit of probabilistic compute (P0).
250	
251	Binding of the bounded step. FOUNDATIONS P0 lets a
252	profile bind the bounded step to its own traversal unit and names
253	[PROFILES §2](PROFILES.md#2-graph-execution), which indexes this profile,
254	as the keeper of that binding. Direction: from the step of
255	FOUNDATIONS P0 to one declared ODD vector or edge traversal. Preserved
256	meaning: the step's selected context fits the actor's envelope, the
257	actor's internal path within the step is its own, and the traversal is
258	the admissible external space. Narrowed scope: one declared vector or edge
259	traversal of a published graph. Invalidation: a change to FOUNDATIONS P0,
260	to the vector's declaration or to the selected basis invalidates the
261	binding until it is evaluated again (P0, P1).
262	
263	The vector declares the admissible external traversal space: required
264	upstream assets; target asset or output contract; required context; role
265	or capability expectation; governing evaluators and gates; provenance
266	obligation; and the lawful stop, hold, gap, continuation or completion
267	states. The runtime may govern, invoke, observe and classify the traversal; it
268	does not own the worker's hidden constructive path. Whatever the traversal
269	boundary does not constrain remains worker-internal HOW: hidden LLM
270	reasoning, heuristic search, domain implementation strategy, tool-local
271	execution detail and product-specific business choice (P0, P6).
272	
273	The classifications of work inside one traversal bind two profile
274	specialisations and one common import. Equal spelling alone establishes
275	none of those relations (P1, P3):
276	
277	- `F_P` (`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-p`) is the shorthand for the
278	  bounded probabilistic worker turn. It specialises substrate-neutral
279	  lawful probabilistic processing: it keeps bounded non-human construction
280	  under declared policy and narrows that meaning to one graph traversal
281	  contract.
282	- `F_D` imports `urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d` from
283	  [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#5-traversals-and-functor-kinds)
284	  in the exact complete STDO release selected by the application, including
285	  its immutable calculus edition. It adds the graph traversal's operation
286	  contract, scope and authority, not another definition of the kind.
287	  Existing evaluation and proof operations retain the unchanged-subject
288	  evaluation profile; admission and construction operations retain their
289	  own evidence contracts and grants. Use of the common kind is conditional
290	  on the total-domain eligibility assessment in
291	  [RELEASE §9](RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration). Domain-local
292	  optimization or validation moves no domain HOW into the graph language, the runtime or the
293	  framework and grants no broader consequences.
294	- `F_H` (`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-h`) is the shorthand for
295	  explicit human adjudication invoked under the traversal's declared
296	  authority and ambiguity policy. It specialises the substrate-neutral
297	  human-adjudication concept and grants a human no ambient traversal,
298	  semantic or closure authority.
299	
300	F_P and F_H are the two declared specialisations that PROFILES §1 requires. The F_P
301	specialisation runs from
302	`urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:lawful-probabilistic-processing` to
303	`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-p`; the F_H specialisation runs from
304	`urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:human-adjudication` to
305	`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-h`. The source concepts and their
306	context are owned by
307	[SPEC_METHOD §5](SPEC_METHOD.md#5-ambiguity-governance-and-lifecycle); this
308	profile owns the targets in the graph-native ODD context (P1, P6).
309	
310	Both relations preserve the source meaning and authority, narrow scope to
311	a declared ODD traversal, and add graph-contract and runtime-control
312	coordinates. They exclude processing or adjudication outside that
313	traversal, refuse ambient worker or human authority, and have no implied
314	inverse. Their source and target basis is the selected complete STDO
315	release, their governed scope is ODD traversal, and this clause is their
316	provenance carrier. A change to either concept or context, to the basis,
317	to the scope, to the preserved or narrowed meaning or to the control
318	contract invalidates the affected specialisation until it is evaluated
319	again (P1, P3, P6).
320	
321	The F_D import runs from the common concept to its use under this profile,
322	preserves the common total deterministic contract, and narrows each use to
323	its declared ODD operation. Its source and target basis is the exact
324	selected complete release; a change to that edition, traversal contract,
325	material dependency, termination evidence or authority invalidates the
326	affected eligibility claim. The former
327	`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-d` remains a historical concept on its
328	legacy edition. It is not an unconditional alias: only the explicit
329	[migration mapping](RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration) licenses a
330	successor use, preserving the original evidence, permissions and results.
331

## 5. Graph model

The product is expressed as a declared asset graph over the state
transitions relevant to the product's work (P0, P3).

### Nodes

Nodes name bounded states of typed domain assets in the workspace. In one software-development ODD product the nodes include
`intent`, `product`, `requirements`, `design`, `module_decomp`, `code`,
`uat_testcases`, `integration_tests`, `bootloader` and build targets. Those
names are illustrative and product-local; the law is that nodes name
bounded states (P3).

### Vectors

Vectors are the lawful transitions between nodes and are the admissible
transitions of the product. Each vector declares its required upstream
assets, its target asset, its governing evaluators and gates, and its
output contract (P4a, P6).

### Probabilistic compute

Probabilistic compute in this profile is bounded constructive work over
one declared vector or edge traversal, where the graph or runtime does not
fully determine the worker's internal solution path. One vector or edge
traversal is the bounded unit of probabilistic compute (P0).

Binding of the bounded step. FOUNDATIONS P0 lets a
profile bind the bounded step to its own traversal unit and names
[PROFILES §2](PROFILES.md#2-graph-execution), which indexes this profile,
as the keeper of that binding. Direction: from the step of
FOUNDATIONS P0 to one declared ODD vector or edge traversal. Preserved
meaning: the step's selected context fits the actor's envelope, the
actor's internal path within the step is its own, and the traversal is
the admissible external space. Narrowed scope: one declared vector or edge
traversal of a published graph. Invalidation: a change to FOUNDATIONS P0,
to the vector's declaration or to the selected basis invalidates the
binding until it is evaluated again (P0, P1).

The vector declares the admissible external traversal space: required
upstream assets; target asset or output contract; required context; role
or capability expectation; governing evaluators and gates; provenance
obligation; and the lawful stop, hold, gap, continuation or completion
states. The runtime may govern, invoke, observe and classify the traversal; it
does not own the worker's hidden constructive path. Whatever the traversal
boundary does not constrain remains worker-internal HOW: hidden LLM
reasoning, heuristic search, domain implementation strategy, tool-local
execution detail and product-specific business choice (P0, P6).

The classifications of work inside one traversal bind two profile
specialisations and one common import. Equal spelling alone establishes
none of those relations (P1, P3):

- `F_P` (`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-p`) is the shorthand for the
  bounded probabilistic worker turn. It specialises substrate-neutral
  lawful probabilistic processing: it keeps bounded non-human construction
  under declared policy and narrows that meaning to one graph traversal
  contract.
- `F_D` imports `urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d` from
  [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#5-traversals-and-functor-kinds)
  in the exact complete STDO release selected by the application, including
  its immutable calculus edition. It adds the graph traversal's operation
  contract, scope and authority, not another definition of the kind.
  Existing evaluation and proof operations retain the unchanged-subject
  evaluation profile; admission and construction operations retain their
  own evidence contracts and grants. Use of the common kind is conditional
  on the total-domain eligibility assessment in
  [RELEASE §9](RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration). Domain-local
  optimization or validation moves no domain HOW into the graph language, the runtime or the
  framework and grants no broader consequences.
- `F_H` (`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-h`) is the shorthand for
  explicit human adjudication invoked under the traversal's declared
  authority and ambiguity policy. It specialises the substrate-neutral
  human-adjudication concept and grants a human no ambient traversal,
  semantic or closure authority.

F_P and F_H are the two declared specialisations that PROFILES §1 requires. The F_P
specialisation runs from
`urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:lawful-probabilistic-processing` to
`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-p`; the F_H specialisation runs from
`urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:human-adjudication` to
`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-h`. The source concepts and their
context are owned by
[SPEC_METHOD §5](SPEC_METHOD.md#5-ambiguity-governance-and-lifecycle); this
profile owns the targets in the graph-native ODD context (P1, P6).

Both relations preserve the source meaning and authority, narrow scope to
a declared ODD traversal, and add graph-contract and runtime-control
coordinates. They exclude processing or adjudication outside that
traversal, refuse ambient worker or human authority, and have no implied
inverse. Their source and target basis is the selected complete STDO
release, their governed scope is ODD traversal, and this clause is their
provenance carrier. A change to either concept or context, to the basis,
to the scope, to the preserved or narrowed meaning or to the control
contract invalidates the affected specialisation until it is evaluated
again (P1, P3, P6).

The F_D import runs from the common concept to its use under this profile,
preserves the common total deterministic contract, and narrows each use to
its declared ODD operation. Its source and target basis is the exact
selected complete release; a change to that edition, traversal contract,
material dependency, termination evidence or authority invalidates the
affected eligibility claim. The former
`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-d` remains a historical concept on its
legacy edition. It is not an unconditional alias: only the explicit
[migration mapping](RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration) licenses a
successor use, preserving the original evidence, permissions and results.

The profile governs the traversal contract, its evidence, its provenance
and its execution authority. It does not make the framework the executor of the
domain's internal solution strategy (P0, P6).

### Graph functions

Graph functions are named constructive programs that realise vectors. A
graph function may realise one outer vector directly, refine one outer
vector into a small inner workflow, or act as a reusable higher-order
library function. The outer vector remains the constitutional contract;
the graph function is the constructive realisation of that contract (P4a,
P0).

Binding of refinement.
[ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement) generalises the
refinement of one outer vector into an inner workflow to any realisation,
lets a refinement carry an earlier output to a later step only through a
declared adapter or specialised contract whose declared domain names it,
and names [PROFILES §2](PROFILES.md#2-graph-execution), which indexes this
profile, as the keeper of the ODD binding. This profile declares the
cumulative carried environment of
[§11.8](#118-cumulative-environment-law-is-mandatory) as that specialised
contract; §11.8 is conserved as profile law and is not generalised into
the core. Direction: from the typed refinement of ACTIVATION §4 to a graph
function that refines one outer vector, with the §11.8 environment as its
specialised contract. Preserved meaning: the outer vector stays the
callable contract; the inner steps conserve it and every applicable
invariant; and each inner function's input satisfies its declared domain
and preconditions, as AC-016 requires. Narrowed scope: one published outer
vector and its declared inner workflow, whose retained functions should
declare `environment.requires`, `environment.provides` and
`environment.carries` (§11.8); a later function's declared domain is its
`environment.requires`, which may require any typed binding available in
the cumulative carried environment, not only the immediately previous
output. Invalidation: a change to ACTIVATION §4, to §11.8, to the outer
vector or to a function's environment declaration invalidates the binding
until it is evaluated again (P4a, P4b, P1).

### Traversal

The workflow is a traversal over the graph: bind the current target;
locate the next admissible vectors; traverse one vector; materialise the
next asset; evaluate the vector's declared obligations against admitted
evidence of that asset and its governing inputs; record the bounded result;
continue while the selected outcome and execution basis permit. A recorded
closure establishes only the obligations and subject it evaluated; current
workspace state and Product acceptance retain their own evidence and authority
(§11.5, §11.5D). The graph is the declared program space of the product (P0, P5).

503	## 10. What an ODD product is
504	
505	An ODD product is a configured graph-native domain product whose constructive
506	work is carried by published graph functions over typed domain assets. Its
507	stable application boundary is (P6, P3):
508	
509	```text
510	App
511	= Bootstrap Surface
512	+ Initialization Surface
513	+ Domain Configuration
514	+ Typed Domain Assets / Nodes
515	+ Graph Function Catalogue
516	+ Graph Module
517	+ Policy Hook Bindings
518	+ Runtime
519	+ Projection / Query Surface
520	+ Proof Surface
521	```
522	
523	The ownership split is read strictly. The two topology subsections below
524	name the default topology of a software-development ODD product in this
525	ecosystem; the product's `stdo_<label>.json` definition under
526	[PRODUCT_DEFINITION](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md) binds the actual locations. At
527	the universal layer this profile commits to the authority split (one WHAT
528	surface, one HOW relation, traversal control with the runtime, domain meaning
529	with the product) and not to directory names; existing projects and other ODD
530	product types may use another layout that keeps the split (P6, P1).
531	
532	The product definition's `reference_frame_bases` bindings carry the
533	evaluation-frame meaning of [REFERENCE_FRAME](REFERENCE_FRAME.md). A runtime
534	frame, attention frame, zoom frame or overlay frame stays a contract owned by
535	that runtime in WHAT and HOW; its name does not enrol it in
536	the project's collective evaluation frame set. A declared evaluation frame
537	may inspect such a runtime frame as its exact subject or coordinate
538	without collapsing the two (P1, P3).
539	
540	### Product specification (software-development topology)
541	
542	The product definition's `what` bindings locate the authoritative WHAT;
543	`specification/` is the default software-development location. It defines
544	intent, product position, goals, requirements and scenarios (P6).
545	
546	### Product realisation (software-development topology)
547	
548	The product definition's `how` bindings locate the authoritative HOW;
549	`build_tenants/` is the default software-development location. It carries
550	design, graph publications, code, tests and local proof surfaces (P6).
551	
552	### Runtime
553	
554	The runtime is the consuming Product's declared authority for traversal
555	control: selecting and invoking an admissible graph step and deciding
556	continuation or re-entry under the graph contract and current grant. It
557	consumes domain policy and evaluation results without redefining them.
558	The concrete runtime Product owns scheduling, worker transport, process
559	supervision, storage, event formats, checkpointing, recovery and any replay
560	mechanism it provides. This profile does not prescribe those mechanisms,
561	their APIs or their type names (P6, P3).
562	
563	The core duties to record needed step-produced facts, evaluate claims on
564	an identified basis and keep authorities separate apply through §11.5D.
565	No runtime record supplies authority over the mutable workspace or a
566	decision owned by another role. DESIGN_MODULE governs software
567	realisation where selected; it cannot change this ownership split.
568	
569	### ODD product
570	
571	The ODD product owns domain asset meaning, graph-function meaning, the
572	published function catalogue, policy overlays, domain query projections,
573	and closure and gap interpretation for its domain (P6, P1).
574	
575	### Query and service layers
576	
577	Service or query layers may own transport, sessions, routing,
578	browser-safe projection and API surfaces. A view grants no traversal
579	control or decision authority. The real constructive carrier is never hidden
580	behind the word service (P6).
581	
582	## 11. Core law
583	
584	An ODD product is built correctly only when every clause of this section
585	holds (P6).
586	
587	### 11.1 Typed assets and nodes are explicit
588	
589	The product works over explicit typed assets or typed nodes. It does not
590	work over one hidden project blob, one giant mutable workspace object or one
591	undocumented service payload. Concrete assets must bind explicitly into
592	typed domain boundaries. Where an asset is a real produced or consumed boundary,
593	its `asset_surface` is declared (P3).
594	
595	### 11.2 Graph functions are the primary constructive carrier
596	
597	Every operative constructive step is carried by one named `GraphFunction`
598	or one lawful graph-function composition. The real carrier is never left
599	inside orchestration loops, bespoke Python pipeline runners, controller
600	scripts, or service methods that only happen to call graph helpers
601	(P0, P4a).
602	
603	### 11.2A Outcome-first realisation order
604	
605	Because this profile makes an edge traversal the unit of compute, an ODD
606	product must use that unit of compute to build its own operative framework
607	behaviour. The required order is: declare the outcome
608	traversal over typed assets; publish the declarative graph and runtime carrier
609	structure; implement only the minimal imperative adapter code that remains
610	necessary (P0, P6).
611	
612	An outcome traversal declares the governed movement before
613	implementation: source asset type; target asset type; edge traversal or
614	graph-function name; closure or evaluation obligation; lineage obligation;
615	ambiguity or gap obligation; allowed `F_D`, `F_P` and `F_H` bindings. The
616	declarative carrier structure is graph functions, typed nodes,
617	vectors, operator bindings, evaluator bindings, carrier schemas, policy
618	declarations, projection declarations and provenance obligations
619	(P0, P3).
620	
621	Imperative adapter code is lawful only where it transports or persists
622	facts: file or network IO; CLI or API transport; event persistence;
623	runtime invocation; projection rendering; tool execution already admitted
624	by a declared traversal. Imperative code must not own domain meaning,
625	semantic target movement, step selection, closure semantics or provenance
626	outside the declared graph contract and authority bindings. Framework behaviour implemented
627	imperatively first and only later described in graph terminology is
628	ODD-shaped but not yet ODD-built (P6, P0).
629	
630	### 11.3 The function catalogue is published
631	
632	The live line must publish a machine-readable function catalogue. At
633	minimum each retained function should expose its name, inputs, outputs,
634	intent, and public or helper role. A callable surface that exists only in
635	prose or in prompt memory leaves the product under-built (P6, P3).
636	
637	### 11.4 The graph module is the operative publication surface
638	
639	The product must publish the public graph-function carriers, the graph or
640	graphs those carriers traverse, typed node and vector surfaces, and the
641	semantic jobs or equivalent outer callable contracts bound to the public
642	carrier. Callers are never bound directly to hidden inner vectors (P4a,
643	P3).
644	
645	Where a public carrier refines into inner executable structure, the live
646	traversal boundaries are published explicitly through declared graph boundary
647	surfaces identifying the refinement or candidate family and its contract.
648	The outer public carrier remains the callable contract (P4a, P3).
649	
650	### 11.5 Workspace truth and runtime projections
651	
652	The mutable workspace and its authoritative inputs are the continuing truth
653	surface under [ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart).
654	Execution records and query views are evidence or derived views of named
655	subjects within that workspace. They do not form a second truth surface
656	and have no independent Product, semantic or acceptance authority (P3, P6).
657	
658	An evaluation may read declared workspace sources directly. It identifies
659	the acquired subject, basis, provenance and validity conditions under the
660	core evidence rules. A source observation need not be copied into a ledger
661	before it can support an evaluation. Whether it is admissible evidence for
662	the declared question is determined by that evaluation's contract (P6).
663	
664	Current-state claims need current evidence. A historical record cannot
665	establish an unobserved present condition, restore a missing asset or
666	resolve conflicting material observations by precedence. Reuse follows
667	ACTIVATION §5 and EVALUATION; raw file presence supplies no decision grant.
668	
669	### 11.5A The runtime owns continuation and re-entry
670	
671	The declared runtime authority controls continuation and re-entry for its
672	traversal. A bounded domain step returns its outputs and result through its
673	published contract. A Product, plugin, service or projection cannot acquire
674	another traversal's control merely by invoking it or reporting its status
675	(P6, P3).
676	
677	The consuming Product defines the concrete continuation protocol. ODD
678	requires explicit ownership and lawful graph transitions, not particular
679	command names, process APIs, evaluator functions or a fixed execution loop.
680	
681	### 11.5B Execution authority audit
682	
683	Before activation and closure, a change to traversal control, delegation
684	(including worker transport and process supervision), admission, evidence
685	evaluation, closure, assurance, retry or continuation must identify the
686	affected authority boundaries and show that each operation
687	has its declared owner and grant. The audit establishes that the runtime
688	governs the affected traversal and no other controller can claim the same
689	authority. It examines the supported call path as well as its outputs;
690	artifact checks alone cannot establish absence of hidden control (P6).
691	Missing or conflicting authority prevents the affected activation and closure.
692	
693	Where an operation admits a consequential transformation, its admission
694	semantics remain with
695	[ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#complete-enclosing-relation-admission).
696	The software-design application remains with
697	[DESIGN_MODULE](DESIGN_MODULE.md#transformation-admission-completeness-up-016).
698	Runtime control, evidence evaluation, operation grants and acceptance
699	are separately bound. The F_P and F_H specialisations of §5 confer no
700	additional authority. The Product supplies the concrete audit inventory
701	and evidence for its execution design (P1, P6).
702	
703	### 11.5C Projection-source coherence
704	
705	A projection names its sources, subject, scope and validity conditions.
706	Function views reconcile to the published graph module; current asset
707	views reconcile to workspace evidence; execution-history views name the
708	records that support their historical claims. Neither matching names nor
709	matching output establishes structural or semantic identity (P3, P6).
710	
711	Missing, stale or materially conflicting sources leave the affected claim
712	unestablished until reconciled. Negative proof for a projection includes
713	material structural drift as well as missing sources. A projection cannot
714	repair its authority basis by reconstructing a competing record.
715	
716	### 11.5D Evidence and bounded decisions
717	
718	Tracking and reconciliation are required functions. Work keeps the current
719	obligations, decisions, progress and unresolved matters available to the
720	actors that need them, and reconciles that account with the mutable
721	workspace and its authoritative inputs before relying on it for a material
722	decision. A changed source, unresolved conflict or stale basis invalidates
723	the affected claim until evaluated again. The account supports coordination;
724	it does not become a second truth surface (P0, P3, P4b, P6).
725	
726	The [generic register example](examples/GENERIC_REGISTER.md) illustrates one
727	tool for those functions. An LLM or other executor may supply an equivalent
728	mechanism. Equivalence is functional: the needed facts remain available
729	across the relevant steps and actors, evidence can be re-acquired by reference,
730	and current claims reconcile to the authoritative workspace. A particular
731	table, file, storage system or register product is not required.
732	
733	The selected outcome comes from
734	[SPEC_METHOD §3](SPEC_METHOD.md#3-outcome-conservation); traversal activity
735	does not select a new outcome. Each invoked step binds its graph contract,
736	inputs, target, obligations, authority and lawful stop conditions. Changes
737	to those commitments re-enter their owning surface under SPEC_METHOD §4
738	(P2, P6).
739	
740	Evidence acquisition follows ACTIVATION §2 and EVALUATION. Evaluations may
741	use current workspace observations and evidence by reference. A declared
742	source that a later actor can re-acquire remains a source; its use in a
743	closure-relevant call does not itself make it a step-produced fact.
744	Where a transient observation cannot be re-acquired and a later step needs
745	it, the producing step records it under
746	[FOUNDATIONS P4b](FOUNDATIONS.md#3-commitments). The same duty applies to
747	needed judgments, residuals and authority decisions (P0, P4b).
748	
749	The record identifies the subject, basis, scope, evidence references and
750	authority that make a decision interpretable. Corrections and supersession
751	retain enough identity to distinguish prior evidence from a current claim.
752	P4b does not require duplication of re-acquirable files, every evaluator
753	input and output, or an immutable log from which every decision can be
754	replayed. A concrete Product may require those facilities for its own
755	outcome; it defines and qualifies them there.
756	
757	A worker produces a candidate under the acquired bounded contract. Its
758	report, an artifact's presence or a successful process exit cannot alone
759	close the traversal or accept the Product. Evaluation, artifact admission
760	and acceptance keep their contracts and owners under ACTIVATION, TICKETS
761	and EVALUATION. A common F_D claim additionally meets §5's total-domain
762	contract and supplies no operation authority by itself (P6).
763	An F_P worker must not be given an F_D-authored semantic extraction recipe
764	when the edge requires F_P judgment (P0, P6).
765	
766	Each evaluation carries its predicate and core result under
767	[FOUNDATIONS Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). Runtime-specific result
768	names and any refinements belong to the consuming Product, which must
769	declare their mapping; this profile defines no closure-decision enum.
770	Evidence for one predicate cannot satisfy another. Missing coverage and
771	material residuals remain visible, and traversal closure does not imply
772	construction availability, Product acceptance or a successor disposition
773	under RELEASE (P5, P6).
774	
775	A material surprise or changed basis returns through ACTIVATION's
776	feedback, diagnosis and re-entry rules. Resumption acquires what the next
777	bounded step needs, including prior step-produced facts and current
778	sources. These obligations apply to inner steps as well as their outer
779	graph contract. The concrete runtime owns the selection algorithm,
780	evaluator decomposition, carrier schemas and recovery protocol; none is
781	fixed by this profile.
782	
783	### 11.6 Product-specific semantics sit above the shared carrier
784	
785	This profile gives the product shape, not the domain semantics. The same
786	ODD structural law can build many different domain products, and each
787	product defines its own asset meanings, proof lanes and query overlays.
788	Structural graph language law and product-specific semantic law are never confused
789	(P1).
790	
791	### 11.7 Manual walkthrough must still be lawful
792	
793	Automation must stay true for a manual walkthrough. A human operator using
794	only the declared authority surfaces should be able to (P0, P6):
795	
796	1. identify the current asset state, the current typed asset or node;
797	2. identify the next lawful vector and its public graph-function carrier,
798	   the vector being the constitutional transition contract and the graph
799	   function the published constructive program that realises it (§5
800	   Vectors and Graph functions);
801	3. determine the required inputs, evaluators, output contract and carried
802	   environment;
803	4. construct or assess the next asset, a produced asset or checkpoint;
804	5. repeat until target-relative closure is reached.
805	
806	Automation may make this faster, safer or more repeatable; it may not
807	invent a different process. Automation is lawful when it renders prompts,
808	scaffolds artifacts, selects the next traversal step, runs workers,
809	collects evidence and assesses closure. Automation is unlawful when it
810	skips undeclared nodes; fabricates authority absent from the declared
811	surfaces; collapses several constitutional transitions into one opaque
812	step without declaring the refinement; depends on implementation-carrier
813	knowledge the installed product should not have; or collapses the
814	installed builder and the product under development into one authority
815	surface during self-host work (P0, P6).
816	
817	If the team cannot explain the manual traversal, the automation is not yet
818	method-safe. Automation that cannot be explained in these terms is ahead
819	of the method (P0, P6).
820	
821	### 11.7A Conforming agentic development
822	
823	This profile is the premise for conforming agentic development over the
824	graph-native workspace. An agentic coder produces governed work by
825	following the constitutional process over a minimal declared authority
826	packet, and admission gates the artifacts it produces. SPEC_METHOD governs
827	the general constitutional process and [TICKETS](TICKETS.md) governs
828	artifact admission; this section names the ODD specialisation and composes
829	that law without declaring it again (P6, P0).
830	
831	Conformance has two halves: an F_P walkthrough supplying evidence that the
832	process can be followed, and a declared admission gate assessing the produced
833	artifacts under its evidence contract and grant. A gate claiming F_D also
834	establishes the common kind's eligibility under §5; its kind is no authority
835	to admit (P6).
836	
837	The walkthrough is the conformance proof. §11.7 requires automation to
838	stay true for a manual walkthrough; its agentic form is a conformance test
839	of the method itself. An agentic coder executes the constitutional process
840	end to end on real work, using only the declared authority surfaces:
841	intake triage, the smallest lawful re-entry, the specification,
842	requirement, design and ticket chain, the evidence and bounded-decision rules of
843	§11.5D, and closure proof. The agentic coder is F_P over the
844	constitutional process (P0, P6).
845	
846	The agent works from a minimal declared authority packet, not from memory
847	and not from wholesale hidden context. The general method already requires
848	declared context for any agentic work unit: input and output contract,
849	required context, role, evaluator regime and provenance (SPEC_METHOD;
850	[ACTIVATION §1](ACTIVATION.md#1-the-step)). The ODD addition is that the

## 10. What an ODD product is

An ODD product is a configured graph-native domain product whose constructive
work is carried by published graph functions over typed domain assets. Its
stable application boundary is (P6, P3):

```text
App
= Bootstrap Surface
+ Initialization Surface
+ Domain Configuration
+ Typed Domain Assets / Nodes
+ Graph Function Catalogue
+ Graph Module
+ Policy Hook Bindings
+ Runtime
+ Projection / Query Surface
+ Proof Surface
```

The ownership split is read strictly. The two topology subsections below
name the default topology of a software-development ODD product in this
ecosystem; the product's `stdo_<label>.json` definition under
[PRODUCT_DEFINITION](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md) binds the actual locations. At
the universal layer this profile commits to the authority split (one WHAT
surface, one HOW relation, traversal control with the runtime, domain meaning
with the product) and not to directory names; existing projects and other ODD
product types may use another layout that keeps the split (P6, P1).

The product definition's `reference_frame_bases` bindings carry the
evaluation-frame meaning of [REFERENCE_FRAME](REFERENCE_FRAME.md). A runtime
frame, attention frame, zoom frame or overlay frame stays a contract owned by
that runtime in WHAT and HOW; its name does not enrol it in
the project's collective evaluation frame set. A declared evaluation frame
may inspect such a runtime frame as its exact subject or coordinate
without collapsing the two (P1, P3).

### Product specification (software-development topology)

The product definition's `what` bindings locate the authoritative WHAT;
`specification/` is the default software-development location. It defines
intent, product position, goals, requirements and scenarios (P6).

### Product realisation (software-development topology)

The product definition's `how` bindings locate the authoritative HOW;
`build_tenants/` is the default software-development location. It carries
design, graph publications, code, tests and local proof surfaces (P6).

### Runtime

The runtime is the consuming Product's declared authority for traversal
control: selecting and invoking an admissible graph step and deciding
continuation or re-entry under the graph contract and current grant. It
consumes domain policy and evaluation results without redefining them.
The concrete runtime Product owns scheduling, worker transport, process
supervision, storage, event formats, checkpointing, recovery and any replay
mechanism it provides. This profile does not prescribe those mechanisms,
their APIs or their type names (P6, P3).

The core duties to record needed step-produced facts, evaluate claims on
an identified basis and keep authorities separate apply through §11.5D.
No runtime record supplies authority over the mutable workspace or a
decision owned by another role. DESIGN_MODULE governs software
realisation where selected; it cannot change this ownership split.

### ODD product

The ODD product owns domain asset meaning, graph-function meaning, the
published function catalogue, policy overlays, domain query projections,
and closure and gap interpretation for its domain (P6, P1).

### Query and service layers

Service or query layers may own transport, sessions, routing,
browser-safe projection and API surfaces. A view grants no traversal
control or decision authority. The real constructive carrier is never hidden
behind the word service (P6).

## 11. Core law

An ODD product is built correctly only when every clause of this section
holds (P6).

### 11.1 Typed assets and nodes are explicit

The product works over explicit typed assets or typed nodes. It does not
work over one hidden project blob, one giant mutable workspace object or one
undocumented service payload. Concrete assets must bind explicitly into
typed domain boundaries. Where an asset is a real produced or consumed boundary,
its `asset_surface` is declared (P3).

### 11.2 Graph functions are the primary constructive carrier

Every operative constructive step is carried by one named `GraphFunction`
or one lawful graph-function composition. The real carrier is never left
inside orchestration loops, bespoke Python pipeline runners, controller
scripts, or service methods that only happen to call graph helpers
(P0, P4a).

### 11.2A Outcome-first realisation order

Because this profile makes an edge traversal the unit of compute, an ODD
product must use that unit of compute to build its own operative framework
behaviour. The required order is: declare the outcome
traversal over typed assets; publish the declarative graph and runtime carrier
structure; implement only the minimal imperative adapter code that remains
necessary (P0, P6).

An outcome traversal declares the governed movement before
implementation: source asset type; target asset type; edge traversal or
graph-function name; closure or evaluation obligation; lineage obligation;
ambiguity or gap obligation; allowed `F_D`, `F_P` and `F_H` bindings. The
declarative carrier structure is graph functions, typed nodes,
vectors, operator bindings, evaluator bindings, carrier schemas, policy
declarations, projection declarations and provenance obligations
(P0, P3).

Imperative adapter code is lawful only where it transports or persists
facts: file or network IO; CLI or API transport; event persistence;
runtime invocation; projection rendering; tool execution already admitted
by a declared traversal. Imperative code must not own domain meaning,
semantic target movement, step selection, closure semantics or provenance
outside the declared graph contract and authority bindings. Framework behaviour implemented
imperatively first and only later described in graph terminology is
ODD-shaped but not yet ODD-built (P6, P0).

### 11.3 The function catalogue is published

The live line must publish a machine-readable function catalogue. At
minimum each retained function should expose its name, inputs, outputs,
intent, and public or helper role. A callable surface that exists only in
prose or in prompt memory leaves the product under-built (P6, P3).

### 11.4 The graph module is the operative publication surface

The product must publish the public graph-function carriers, the graph or
graphs those carriers traverse, typed node and vector surfaces, and the
semantic jobs or equivalent outer callable contracts bound to the public
carrier. Callers are never bound directly to hidden inner vectors (P4a,
P3).

Where a public carrier refines into inner executable structure, the live
traversal boundaries are published explicitly through declared graph boundary
surfaces identifying the refinement or candidate family and its contract.
The outer public carrier remains the callable contract (P4a, P3).

### 11.5 Workspace truth and runtime projections

The mutable workspace and its authoritative inputs are the continuing truth
surface under [ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart).
Execution records and query views are evidence or derived views of named
subjects within that workspace. They do not form a second truth surface
and have no independent Product, semantic or acceptance authority (P3, P6).

An evaluation may read declared workspace sources directly. It identifies
the acquired subject, basis, provenance and validity conditions under the
core evidence rules. A source observation need not be copied into a ledger
before it can support an evaluation. Whether it is admissible evidence for
the declared question is determined by that evaluation's contract (P6).

Current-state claims need current evidence. A historical record cannot
establish an unobserved present condition, restore a missing asset or
resolve conflicting material observations by precedence. Reuse follows
ACTIVATION §5 and EVALUATION; raw file presence supplies no decision grant.

### 11.5A The runtime owns continuation and re-entry

The declared runtime authority controls continuation and re-entry for its
traversal. A bounded domain step returns its outputs and result through its
published contract. A Product, plugin, service or projection cannot acquire
another traversal's control merely by invoking it or reporting its status
(P6, P3).

The consuming Product defines the concrete continuation protocol. ODD
requires explicit ownership and lawful graph transitions, not particular
command names, process APIs, evaluator functions or a fixed execution loop.

### 11.5B Execution authority audit

Before activation and closure, a change to traversal control, delegation
(including worker transport and process supervision), admission, evidence
evaluation, closure, assurance, retry or continuation must identify the
affected authority boundaries and show that each operation
has its declared owner and grant. The audit establishes that the runtime
governs the affected traversal and no other controller can claim the same
authority. It examines the supported call path as well as its outputs;
artifact checks alone cannot establish absence of hidden control (P6).
Missing or conflicting authority prevents the affected activation and closure.

Where an operation admits a consequential transformation, its admission
semantics remain with
[ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#complete-enclosing-relation-admission).
The software-design application remains with
[DESIGN_MODULE](DESIGN_MODULE.md#transformation-admission-completeness-up-016).
Runtime control, evidence evaluation, operation grants and acceptance
are separately bound. The F_P and F_H specialisations of §5 confer no
additional authority. The Product supplies the concrete audit inventory
and evidence for its execution design (P1, P6).

### 11.5C Projection-source coherence

A projection names its sources, subject, scope and validity conditions.
Function views reconcile to the published graph module; current asset
views reconcile to workspace evidence; execution-history views name the
records that support their historical claims. Neither matching names nor
matching output establishes structural or semantic identity (P3, P6).

Missing, stale or materially conflicting sources leave the affected claim
unestablished until reconciled. Negative proof for a projection includes
material structural drift as well as missing sources. A projection cannot
repair its authority basis by reconstructing a competing record.

### 11.5D Evidence and bounded decisions

Tracking and reconciliation are required functions. Work keeps the current
obligations, decisions, progress and unresolved matters available to the
actors that need them, and reconciles that account with the mutable
workspace and its authoritative inputs before relying on it for a material
decision. A changed source, unresolved conflict or stale basis invalidates
the affected claim until evaluated again. The account supports coordination;
it does not become a second truth surface (P0, P3, P4b, P6).

The [generic register example](examples/GENERIC_REGISTER.md) illustrates one
tool for those functions. An LLM or other executor may supply an equivalent
mechanism. Equivalence is functional: the needed facts remain available
across the relevant steps and actors, evidence can be re-acquired by reference,
and current claims reconcile to the authoritative workspace. A particular
table, file, storage system or register product is not required.

The selected outcome comes from
[SPEC_METHOD §3](SPEC_METHOD.md#3-outcome-conservation); traversal activity
does not select a new outcome. Each invoked step binds its graph contract,
inputs, target, obligations, authority and lawful stop conditions. Changes
to those commitments re-enter their owning surface under SPEC_METHOD §4
(P2, P6).

Evidence acquisition follows ACTIVATION §2 and EVALUATION. Evaluations may
use current workspace observations and evidence by reference. A declared
source that a later actor can re-acquire remains a source; its use in a
closure-relevant call does not itself make it a step-produced fact.
Where a transient observation cannot be re-acquired and a later step needs
it, the producing step records it under
[FOUNDATIONS P4b](FOUNDATIONS.md#3-commitments). The same duty applies to
needed judgments, residuals and authority decisions (P0, P4b).

The record identifies the subject, basis, scope, evidence references and
authority that make a decision interpretable. Corrections and supersession
retain enough identity to distinguish prior evidence from a current claim.
P4b does not require duplication of re-acquirable files, every evaluator
input and output, or an immutable log from which every decision can be
replayed. A concrete Product may require those facilities for its own
outcome; it defines and qualifies them there.

A worker produces a candidate under the acquired bounded contract. Its
report, an artifact's presence or a successful process exit cannot alone
close the traversal or accept the Product. Evaluation, artifact admission
and acceptance keep their contracts and owners under ACTIVATION, TICKETS
and EVALUATION. A common F_D claim additionally meets §5's total-domain
contract and supplies no operation authority by itself (P6).
An F_P worker must not be given an F_D-authored semantic extraction recipe
when the edge requires F_P judgment (P0, P6).

Each evaluation carries its predicate and core result under
[FOUNDATIONS Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). Runtime-specific result
names and any refinements belong to the consuming Product, which must
declare their mapping; this profile defines no closure-decision enum.
Evidence for one predicate cannot satisfy another. Missing coverage and
material residuals remain visible, and traversal closure does not imply
construction availability, Product acceptance or a successor disposition
under RELEASE (P5, P6).

A material surprise or changed basis returns through ACTIVATION's
feedback, diagnosis and re-entry rules. Resumption acquires what the next
bounded step needs, including prior step-produced facts and current
sources. These obligations apply to inner steps as well as their outer
graph contract. The concrete runtime owns the selection algorithm,
evaluator decomposition, carrier schemas and recovery protocol; none is
fixed by this profile.

### 11.6 Product-specific semantics sit above the shared carrier

This profile gives the product shape, not the domain semantics. The same
ODD structural law can build many different domain products, and each
product defines its own asset meanings, proof lanes and query overlays.
Structural graph language law and product-specific semantic law are never confused
(P1).

### 11.7 Manual walkthrough must still be lawful

Automation must stay true for a manual walkthrough. A human operator using
only the declared authority surfaces should be able to (P0, P6):

1. identify the current asset state, the current typed asset or node;
2. identify the next lawful vector and its public graph-function carrier,
   the vector being the constitutional transition contract and the graph
   function the published constructive program that realises it (§5
   Vectors and Graph functions);
3. determine the required inputs, evaluators, output contract and carried
   environment;
4. construct or assess the next asset, a produced asset or checkpoint;
5. repeat until target-relative closure is reached.

Automation may make this faster, safer or more repeatable; it may not
invent a different process. Automation is lawful when it renders prompts,
scaffolds artifacts, selects the next traversal step, runs workers,
collects evidence and assesses closure. Automation is unlawful when it
skips undeclared nodes; fabricates authority absent from the declared
surfaces; collapses several constitutional transitions into one opaque
step without declaring the refinement; depends on implementation-carrier
knowledge the installed product should not have; or collapses the
installed builder and the product under development into one authority
surface during self-host work (P0, P6).

If the team cannot explain the manual traversal, the automation is not yet
method-safe. Automation that cannot be explained in these terms is ahead
of the method (P0, P6).

### 11.7A Conforming agentic development

This profile is the premise for conforming agentic development over the
graph-native workspace. An agentic coder produces governed work by
following the constitutional process over a minimal declared authority
packet, and admission gates the artifacts it produces. SPEC_METHOD governs
the general constitutional process and [TICKETS](TICKETS.md) governs
artifact admission; this section names the ODD specialisation and composes
that law without declaring it again (P6, P0).

Conformance has two halves: an F_P walkthrough supplying evidence that the
process can be followed, and a declared admission gate assessing the produced
artifacts under its evidence contract and grant. A gate claiming F_D also
establishes the common kind's eligibility under §5; its kind is no authority
to admit (P6).

The walkthrough is the conformance proof. §11.7 requires automation to
stay true for a manual walkthrough; its agentic form is a conformance test
of the method itself. An agentic coder executes the constitutional process
end to end on real work, using only the declared authority surfaces:
intake triage, the smallest lawful re-entry, the specification,
requirement, design and ticket chain, the evidence and bounded-decision rules of
§11.5D, and closure proof. The agentic coder is F_P over the
constitutional process (P0, P6).

The agent works from a minimal declared authority packet, not from memory
and not from wholesale hidden context. The general method already requires
declared context for any agentic work unit: input and output contract,
required context, role, evaluator regime and provenance (SPEC_METHOD;
[ACTIVATION §1](ACTIVATION.md#1-the-step)). The ODD addition is that the
packet carries only the smallest declared authority sufficient to decide
the step, with its source refs, and that conformance is enforced by
admitting the produced artifact rather than by enlarging what the agent
must hold. Compression is prompt input and never the deciding authority
(P0, P6). What a derived surface may decide is owned by

Acquisition and Standalone scope; this section adds only the ODD limit
that follows. A derived surface or projected frame of the general method may
orient the agent to source precedence, lawful re-entry and traceability;
it must not be used to decide product-specific behaviour, which must come
from the current product authority packet (P6, P1).

The walkthrough proves at two levels. The work it produces must be lawful:
correct change class, traceable, admitted. A point where the walkthrough
cannot proceed is a method defect only when a competent agent, correctly
configured and using the declared authority, still cannot decide because
of ambiguity, a missing step, contradictory authority or an undecidable

§11.7 (P6, P5).

An agent that ignored the declared authority, relied on stale memory or
reasoned badly has produced agent error, not a method defect. Admission

becomes law nor silently indicts the method (P6).

This proof is independent of any automated runtime. A live lane that
depends on external execution conditions, such as an overloaded model API
or a flaky transport, cannot prove the constitutional process sound,
because it conflates process validity with runtime availability. The
walkthrough proves the process; the runtime only executes it (P6, P5).

The validator is the conformance gate. The constitutional process is an
interface contract, and interface conformance is enforced by validating
artifacts against the contract, not by the conformer holding the contract.
This profile does not declare the artifact rules again: tickets,
change-class declarations, design-module derivations and execution
contracts are admitted under SPEC_METHOD and TICKETS, which already require
a drafted classification to be admitted or rejected against deterministic
criteria rather than taken as automatic truth. This profile requires only
that agentic development pass through that admission. The agentic coder
produces the artifact; the declared admission gates it deterministically,

enforced by its constructor (§11.1) (P6, P3).

This keeps the F_P and F_D split at the method layer. The agentic coder is
F_P: it reasons, drafts and proposes within the declared packet. Admission
uses F_D only when the §5 total-domain contract is established, and its own
contract and authority determine what artifact-conformance decision it may
make. An unresolved eligibility assessment stays open under the migration
relation; an unchanged-subject evaluator still preserves that subject. The walkthrough
establishes that the process can be followed; admission establishes that
each act of following it conforms (P6, P0).

Conformance is not approval by usage. A passed admission and a completed
walkthrough are conformance evidence, not ratification. Shared method
change still follows §9: repeated agentic execution does not make grey
work constitutional. The agentic coder conforms to the method; it does not
amend the method by acting (P6).

### 11.7B Real authority-path negative proof (STDO-UP-010)

Negative proof for an ODD or graph-native boundary exercises the supported
Product authority path. It must not manufacture the refusal state, blocked
event, gap or verdict that the system is supposed to derive (P6, P5).

Closure-grade negative evidence identifies the supported entry and the
governing authority; invalidates the real authority-bearing input;
exercises the supported path; proves refusal before the prohibited
effect; and establishes that no legacy, fallback, reconstruction or
parallel path succeeds. Source, packaged, installed and runtime absence
are distinct claims (P6, P3).

Where these identities apply, the supported relation is (P6, P4a):

```text
public entry
  -> admitted graph composition owns traversal topology
  -> named GraphFunction supplies the callable work contract
  -> implementation or plugin binding realizes only its admitted seam
  -> the declared runtime governs traversal and continuation
  -> a projection names the workspace evidence supporting its claims
  -> typed Product outcome or continuation
```

No CLI, SDK, service, adapter, plugin, fixture, query or projection may
become a rival traversal controller. The consumer owns the concrete test
and evidence mechanism; this section owns the property that mechanism
must prove (P6).

208	
209	```text
210	Goals → Intent → Product Definition → Requirements → Design → Code
211	  → Events → Projection → Delta → Scenarios → Gap analysis
212	  → Repricing at the layer its change class names
213	```
214	
215	Goals identify the current epics or bounded work wave being pursued toward
216	the Product. Intent defines purpose and direction. Product Definition defines
217	the intended Product end state, including capabilities still to be built,
218	its key terms and its boundaries, in terms that requirements decompose and
219	make true.
220	Requirements define invariant truths the system must satisfy. Design
221	defines the structural decisions, interfaces, carrier surfaces and delivery
222	topology that make those truths achievable; ADRs are one durable form of
223	design record, not a second constitutional layer above design. Code
224	realises those decisions where the selected execution environment is
225	software; a performed human procedure realises them where it is a human
226	process, and both where it is mixed (§11). Events are the retained
227	record of what happened, in the carrier the binding selects: an event

### Constitutional chain

```text
Goals → Intent → Product Definition → Requirements → Design → Code
  → Events → Projection → Delta → Scenarios → Gap analysis
  → Repricing at the layer its change class names
```

Goals identify the current epics or bounded work wave being pursued toward
the Product. Intent defines purpose and direction. Product Definition defines
the intended Product end state, including capabilities still to be built,
its key terms and its boundaries, in terms that requirements decompose and
make true.
Requirements define invariant truths the system must satisfy. Design
defines the structural decisions, interfaces, carrier surfaces and delivery
topology that make those truths achievable; ADRs are one durable form of
design record, not a second constitutional layer above design. Code
realises those decisions where the selected execution environment is
software; a performed human procedure realises them where it is a human
process, and both where it is mixed (§11). Events are the retained
record of what happened, in the carrier the binding selects: an event
stream, a ledger, a signed record or an observation log. Projection
reconstructs current truth from that retained record where the record is
sufficient for the product's obligations; it need not replay a complete
event stream. Delta reveals drift
between intended truth and realised state. Scenarios test operational
meaning: whether the system can do what the words describe. Gap analysis
identifies where real use cases hit the current model and reveal
insufficiency. Repricing updates goals, intent, product, requirements,
design or code when the system no longer harmonises; when gap analysis
reveals constitutional insufficiency, repricing re-enters at the layer its
[change class](#change-classes) names and generates new goals or intent
where the work wave, direction or scope changes (P2, P1).

This is the homeostatic loop. Every link is load-bearing. A break at any
link, goals with no downstream repricing path, an unowned requirement, an
ungrounded design record, code without a design decision, creates
accidental law (P6). Load-bearing means owned, not software: the links
Code, Events and Projection name responsibilities every realisation
carries in the carrier its binding selects (§11), and no product owes a
code base or an event store that its binding does not select (P2, P6).

The goals surface is the bounded work-wave surface: it identifies the current
epics being pursued toward the Product, keeps temporary focus out of
deeper constitutional layers until it is intentionally repriced there, and
is more immediate than intent while remaining higher-level than product
definition and requirements. The product-definition surface is the bridge
between direction and obligation: it states the intended Product end state
under the definition currently in force. Present-tense declarations describe
that adopted destination; implementation status and delivery claims need their
own evidence. The definition names the product terms and boundaries that
downstream layers rely on and provides the surface that requirements decompose.
It is not the immutable release cut
and not the installed product; those are the lineage objects of FOUNDATIONS
§2 (P3).

Requirements are the constitutional what of the project. They are not
limited to user-visible features: the live requirement surface may include
capabilities, invariants, constraints, governance and verification
obligations; what matters is that each requirement states something the
project must make true. Design is the structural how: it chooses the
concrete realisation that satisfies requirement truth, interfaces, topology,
file placement, carrier documents, entry and control surfaces, runtime
wiring and lawful tenant boundaries. Requirements may require such surfaces
to exist and be delivered; design chooses where and how they are realised
unless the path itself is constitutional (P2, P1).

The relation between the WHAT and the build tenants that realise it is
[§11](#11-build-tenant-binding) (P2).

### Manifesto

The method commits to these (P2, P6). It defines the
current goals for the active body of work before repricing deeper
constitutional layers. It works from intent before implementation. It
defines the intended Product end state, including capabilities still to be
built, before decomposing it into detailed requirements. It defines the full
constitutional what in requirements, not merely a feature list. It prefers
declaring desired truth and lawful boundaries over prescribing step-by-step
imperative procedure. It makes design the explicit structural bridge
